additional_concerns: Paragraph 10 establishes continuing ultimate responsibility despite outsourcing. It does not expressly prescribe the candidate's three-part test of retained authority, supervision and satisfactory outcomes; that operational interpretation needs justification and an applicable standard.

No provider-specific facts or assessment period are supplied. Neither retained authority nor accurate vendor records alone establishes substantive fulfillment; missing evidence does not establish substantive failure.
The excerpts supply no severity, duration or remediation rules. Ultimate responsibility must not silently become a universal guarantee against every operational incident.

Part A of the Tokenised Securities Circular Appendix, the complete requirements of paragraphs 10–13 and footnote 2 are absent. Obtain these materials where necessary to determine applicable operational and record-keeping standards; no external dependency IDs are supplied.

Paragraphs 15 and 16 separately condition obtaining third-party audit or verification and a satisfactory legal opinion on SFC request. Their absence does not independently decide paragraph 10 fulfillment.

The supplied register provisions permit specified register-maintenance actors while footnote 1 preserves Product Provider responsibility. The intermediary issuance provision likewise preserves responsibility despite outsourcing, but its actor and activity conditions cannot automatically be imported.
No executable meaning is supplied. Retrieval and the unsupported structural check establish neither legal sufficiency nor implementation fidelity.
